sources.entry: NearDrop - An unofficial Google Nearby Share/Quick Share app for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/localsend/localsend) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: NearDrop is an unofficial, partial macOS implementation of Google's Nearby Share / Quick Share that lets Android devices send files and links to a Mac over the local Wi-Fi network.
summary.what_it_does: It runs as a menu bar app on macOS and saves files received from Android devices into the Downloads folder. Mac users can send files via Finder's Share menu, and send links via the File menu or Safari's share button. Android devices must be on the same Wi-Fi LAN as the Mac, and the Mac is visible to everyone on that network while the app runs. Sending from the Mac to Android requires scanning a QR code NearDrop generates, or using an Android intent shortcut. The README also explains why AirDrop-to-Android is not feasible, pointing to Apple's proprietary AWDL protocol.
use_cases: receive files from an Android phone on a Mac
send files from a Mac to Android via Quick Share
share links from a Mac to an Android device
transfer files between Android and macOS on the same Wi-Fi
replace AirDrop-style sharing for Android phones
how_to_run: Download the latest build from the releases section, unzip, and move the app to the Applications folder.
Right-click the app and select "Open" before the first run, then confirm.
Alternatively, use Sentinel to bypass Gatekeeper.
Or install with Homebrew: brew install grishka/grishka/neardrop && sudo xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/NearDrop.app"
notable: Implements Google Nearby Share / Quick Share protocol partially, in a menu bar app
Receives files into the Downloads folder without extra setup
Sends files via the macOS Finder Share menu
Android-to-Mac discovery works via QR code or intent shortcut, since macOS cannot send the BLE broadcasts Android needs
Protocol documentation is said to be available separately
caveats: Wi-Fi LAN only; no Wi-Fi Direct, hotspot, Bluetooth, or internet WebRTC transport, and public networks such as coffee shops or hotels may block discovery
The app is not notarized or on the Mac App Store, so it triggers Gatekeeper warnings on first run
Mac is visible to all devices on the network while running; Android-to-Mac visibility requires Android's public visibility setting
keywords: share files with my android phone
send files to mac from android
receive files from phone on mac
